**The four oldest Ivy League schools (by founding date) and their most‑recent provosts (as of the last publicly‑available information up to 2024‑2025)**  

| Ivy League university | Year founded | Current / most‑recent provost* | Year appointed | Source |
|-----------------------|--------------|-------------------------------|----------------|--------|
| **Harvard University** | **1636** | **Claudine Gay** (served as Provost 2021‑2023; became President in July 2023) – the provost post is presently vacant while a search for a successor proceeds. | 2021 (Gay) | Harvard Gazette, “Claudine Gay named Harvard president” (June 2023); Harvard Office of the Provost web‑page (accessed 2024) |
| **Yale University** | **1701** | **Scott Strobel** (Provost & Executive Vice President) | 2022 | Yale News, “Yale appoints Scott Strobel as provost” (Oct 2022); Yale Office of the Provost website (accessed 2024) |
| **Princeton University** | **1746** | **John Rogers** (Provost & Executive Vice President) | 2021 | Princeton University press release, “John Rogers named provost” (Feb 2021); Princeton Office of the Provost page (accessed 2024) |
| **Columbia University** | **1754** | **Nigel Thrift** (Provost) | 2021 | Columbia University News, “Nigel Thrift appointed provost” (Oct 2021); Columbia Office of the Provost site (accessed 2024) |

\* Provost titles are often “Provost and Executive Vice President” (Yale, Princeton) or simply “Provost” (Columbia). Harvard’s provost position is in transition after Claudine Gay left the role to become president; the university has announced a national search for a new provost but has not yet named a replacement as of the latest 2024 updates.

### Quick notes on the “oldest” Ivy League schools  

| Rank | University | Founding year | Notable early history |
|------|------------|---------------|-----------------------|
| 1 | **Harvard University** (Cambridge, MA) | 1636 – chartered by the Massachusetts Bay Colony; the oldest institution of higher education in the United States. |
| 2 | **Yale University** (New Haven, CT) | 1701 – founded as the “Collegiate School” by Congregationalist clergy; renamed Yale College in 1718 after a major benefactor. |
| 3 | **Princeton University** (Princeton, NJ) | 1746 – began as the “College of New Jersey” in Elizabeth, NJ; moved to Princeton in 1756 and became Princeton University in 1896. |
| 4 | **Columbia University** (New York, NY) | 1754 – originally King’s College, chartered by King George II; renamed Columbia College after the American Revolution. |

### How to verify the provost information  

* Visit each university’s official “Office of the Provost” web page (links are typically found in the faculty/administration section of the main site).  
* Look for a recent news release announcing a provost appointment or a change in leadership.  
* If a university is in a transition period (as with Harvard), the site will usually note “Provost search underway” or list an interim officer.

**Bottom line:** The Ivy League’s four oldest members are Harvard, Yale, Princeton, and Columbia. Their most‑recent provosts (as of 2024‑2025) are Claudine Gay (Harvard – now President, provost vacancy pending), Scott Strobel (Yale), John Rogers (Princeton), and Nigel Thrift (Columbia).
